To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) HIV and TB are closely linked, with TB being one of the most common opportunistic infections in people with HIV; 2) HIV infection increases the risk of active TB, and the risk is higher in people living with HIV than in those with a negative HIV test; and 3) TB infection increases the risk for HIV acquisition and HIV transmission, and this risk is higher among people with TB than those without TB infection.
The HIV and TB epidemics have been closely linked for decades, and the link has been strengthened in the past decade by the emergence of drug-resistant TB.
